#### New Kenosha hub significantly expands G10 Fulfillment’s Midwest warehouse capacity

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

· Wednesday, September 02, 2026 

 Flexport’s expansion into Canada and the UK aims to give shippers another way to position inventory closer to consumers while tariffs, origin rules and tougher customs enforcement make international supply chains increasingly complex. (Photo: Jim Allen/FreightWaves) 

Flexport has launched its first fulfillment operations outside the U.S., expanding into Canada and the United Kingdom as shifting tariffs and tougher customs enforcement reshape global supply chains.

The San Francisco-based logistics provider announced Tuesday that fulfillment services are now available in Mississauga, Ontario, and Manchester, England, aiming to allow customers to hold inventory closer to end consumers.
